- Overestimate early in the forecast horizon when sentiment is negative (especially if recent sentiment is > -0.10), as models tend to underreact to bearish signals.
- Underestimate when sentiment is strongly positive and recent prices are rising — models often lag in capturing momentum.
- Avoid sharp upward spikes in forecast after a recent price spike; true outcomes often show mean reversion or consolidation within 3–5 days.
- When sentiment is consistently negative over 3+ days, model forecasts should be adjusted downward by 0.5–1.5% of the 30d average to account for risk aversion.
- Forecast horizon 30d is prone to over-optimism in the first 10 days — true outcomes often diverge significantly in the middle to end of the horizon.
- If sentiment history shows a recent reversal (e.g., from negative to positive), model should not immediately overcorrect — allow 2–3 days of lag before adjusting upward.
- When sentiment is neutral or mildly positive, model should not assume continuation of trend — true outcomes often show mean reversion or sideways movement.
